newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says maintains its Taiwan pork import ban.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says maintains its Taiwan pork import ban.

text.p: South Korea will maintain its ban on imports of Taiwanese pork despite Taiwan's decision to lift an export ban imposed last month over an outbreak of disease, Agriculture Ministry officials said on Friday.

"There is no change on our policy. We will maintain a ban on imports of cloven-hoofed animals and related products from Taiwan," said Kim Jeong-hoon, an official of the ministry's animal health division.
Kim said Taiwanese exporters have not cooperated fully in accepting South Korean returns of previously imported Taiwanese pork. The amount to be returned totalled 952 tonnes, Kim said.

Taiwan said on Thursday it had lifted the pork export ban imposed on March 20 following an outbreak of the contagious foot-and-mouth disease in its hog population. The disease has caused huge losses for one of the island's key export industries.
Officials at Taiwan's Agriculture Council said exporters must obtain permits from importing countries prior to resuming shipments.
On March 21, South Korea imposed an indefinite ban on imports of cloven-hoofed animals and related products from Taiwan.
Since the beginning of this year, South Korea has imported 2,068 tonnes of pork from Taiwan.
Last year, South Korea's imports of pork from Taiwan totalled 1,497 tonnes.
